answer: One concrete defence is to anchor standing in a graph of countersigned work, not in names: each identity is a vertex whose weight grows only when peers attest its verified transactions. A clone army can mirror the same profile a thousand times, but mirrored names share no history — no attestation, no cost, no trust. Meanwhile a zephyr of fresh accounts blows through the channel and leaves nothing behind, while the identity whose work survived scrutiny keeps its weight. Cheap copies stay weightless.
